messages.content: The Dallas team came back. The restaurant is in Addison, near Belt Line and the Tollway, and the regional office is by DFW on the Irving side. So downtown looks wrong. Compare the suggested hotel with better-positioned options for Monday and Tuesday nights, September 15 and 16.
That confirms the downtown location would create unnecessary driving. What is the reimbursable ceiling for the two-night stay, and how late does cancellation need to remain available?
Keep the full hotel charge at or under $500, including taxes. I need to be able to cancel through Sunday evening because the opening schedule could still move.

I’ll compare the downtown suggestion with properties around Las Colinas and the north DFW corridor. Those areas split the difference better between Addison and the Irving office. I’ll use refundable rates only and show the complete two-night charge rather than the headline nightly rate.
Good. I don’t need breakfast or anything elaborate. A reliable business hotel with parking is enough.

The suggested Hyatt Regency Dallas is $219 per night plus taxes, or $498.34 total for two nights. Cancellation is allowed until 11:59 p.m. Sunday, September 14, and self-parking adds $25 per night, bringing the effective trip cost to $548.34. Typical weekday driving is about 30-45 minutes to Addison and 20-30 minutes to the Irving office, with greater exposure to downtown traffic.
So it technically fits only before parking and is the worst location. Drop it unless the alternatives are meaningfully worse.

Three better-positioned refundable options fit the stated ceiling. Aloft Las Colinas is $438.12 total with free self-parking and cancellation through 11:59 p.m. Sunday. Hilton Garden Inn Las Colinas is $466.40 total with free parking and the same Sunday cancellation cutoff. DoubleTree by Hilton DFW Airport North is $421.26 total with free parking, but free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. Saturday.
Give me the drive comparison. Monday night I’ll come from DFW, Tuesday I need Addison first and then the Irving office, and Wednesday I’ll start at the office before going back to Addison.

Aloft Las Colinas is roughly 12-18 minutes from DFW after the Monday arrival, 18-25 minutes to the Addison site, and 8-12 minutes to the Irving office. Hilton Garden Inn Las Colinas is about 15-20 minutes from DFW, 15-22 minutes to Addison, and 12-16 minutes to the office. DoubleTree DFW Airport North is about 8-12 minutes from the terminals, 25-35 minutes to Addison, and 12-18 minutes to the office.
The DoubleTree saves money, but that Addison leg happens twice and the cancellation is earlier than I asked for.

Right. It saves $16.86 versus the Aloft, but could add roughly 15-25 minutes of driving across the two Addison trips, and its Saturday cancellation deadline misses your Sunday-evening requirement. I would not keep it as a finalist unless airport proximity becomes the deciding factor.
No. Remove it. Compare the two Las Colinas hotels more closely, including the actual room terms.

Aloft Las Colinas: one king room, $189 Monday and $189 Tuesday, plus $60.12 in taxes, for $438.12 total. Wi-Fi and outdoor self-parking are included. The rate is pay at property, with no deposit, and cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. Sunday; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The room has a work desk and mini-fridge. Hilton Garden Inn Las Colinas: one king room, $201 Monday and $201 Tuesday, plus $64.40 in taxes, for $466.40 total. Wi-Fi and self-parking are included. It is also pay at property, cancellable through 11:59 p.m. Sunday, with a one-night-plus-tax late cancellation penalty. The room includes a desk, mini-fridge, microwave, and coffee maker.
Any issue with late arrival Monday? The flight gets in at 8:42, but I probably won’t reach either hotel until after 10.

Both have 24-hour front desks and accept a late arrival. The reservation should include an estimated arrival of 10:15-10:45 p.m. so the hotel does not treat the room as an uncertain no-show if the flight is delayed.
Which one is quieter and which one gives me the easier Tuesday morning?

The Hilton Garden Inn is in a more conventional office-park setting and recent room descriptions indicate a quieter layout away from the lobby. It is also a few minutes closer to Addison in typical morning traffic. The Aloft is closer to the Irving office and costs $28.28 less, but its lobby and common areas are more active. At either hotel, requesting a room away from the elevator and main road would reduce noise risk.
I’m leaning Hilton Garden Inn because Tuesday starts in Addison. But Wednesday’s flight choice still depends on whether they finish at 4:30 or 5:30, correct?

Correct. The hotel works with either return flight. If Wednesday ends firmly at 4:30, the provisional 8:20 p.m. DFW-ORD nonstop remains workable. If it may run until 5:30, the 9:45 p.m. nonstop is the safer option. Neither flight is booked.
Before I decide, quantify the Wednesday difference from each hotel. I’ll check out, go to the Irving office, then Addison, then DFW.

The morning hotel-to-office leg favors Aloft by about 4-6 minutes: roughly 8-12 minutes versus 12-16 from Hilton Garden Inn. From the office to Addison, and later Addison to DFW, the routing is effectively the same regardless of hotel because you will already have checked out. Across the whole Wednesday sequence, Aloft’s advantage is therefore only those few minutes in the morning.
Then keep Hilton Garden Inn first and Aloft second. I’m not booking until the team confirms Wednesday, but I want the exact two finalists captured with costs and cancellation.

Finalists retained for September 15-17: 1. Hilton Garden Inn Las Colinas, king room, $466.40 total including taxes, free self-parking, pay at property, and free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. Sunday, September 14. It is about 15-22 minutes to the Addison site and 12-16 minutes to the Irving office. 2. Aloft Las Colinas, king room, $438.12 total including taxes, free self-parking, pay at property, and free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. Sunday, September 14. It is about 18-25 minutes to Addison and 8-12 minutes to the office. Hilton Garden Inn is the lead because Tuesday begins in Addison and the expected setting is quieter; Aloft saves $28.28 and shortens the office drive. No hotel or Dallas flight has been booked. The remaining action is the local team’s confirmation of Wednesday’s firm end time, which determines whether to pair the hotel with the 8:20 p.m. or 9:45 p.m. return.
